data.exact_reserve_text: A positive run-off of GBP 12.1m on the 2014 and prior years' reserves (2013 and prior: GBP 17.1m) was experienced in the year. This change to the previous closed year reserves was 4.9% of the relevant provisions brought forward.

prior_year_events.event_name: Reduction in assessment of medical malpractice claims (State Volunteer and NECC contracts)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Reduction in assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2014 and prior accounts following improvements in State Volunteer and NECC contracts during 2017, producing favourable development on those prior years.

named_events.loss_description: Across all years of account projecting ultimate gross catastrophe losses of GBP 61.0m, with a year-end incurred of GBP 41.0m. Ultimate net losses are projected to be GBP 42.8m, 92% of which is estimated to fall to the 2017 year of account.
Mentioned as one of the major 2017 events (alongside Harvey and the Caribbean); contributed to calendar year losses and catastrophe exposure.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a gross favourable prior-year run-off of GBP 12.1m on 2014 and prior underwriting years, primarily driven by favourable development in medical malpractice claims (improvements in State Volunteer and NECC contracts). On a gross basis this represents a c.3.5% release of opening gross claims reserves. Separately, the 2017 catastrophe season (Harvey, Irma, Maria and Californian wildfires) generated substantial gross and net catastrophe losses in 2017, but these relate mainly to the current year of account.
raw_causal_phrases: A positive run-off of GBP 12.1m on the 2014 and prior years' reserves (2013 and prior: GBP 17.1m) was experienced in the year.

there has been an overall net surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 2.9m (2016: GBP 20.1m) due to lower than expected incurred movements across most classes of business. This was primarily due to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2014 and prior accounts following improvements in State Volunteer and NECC contracts during 2017.

Across all years of account we are projecting ultimate gross catastrophe losses of GBP 61.0m, with a year-end incurred of GBP 41.0m. Ultimate net losses are projected to be GBP 42.8m, 92% of which is estimated to fall to the 2017 year of account.
data.data_quality_notes: Primary gross prior-year movement (GBP 12.1m release) taken from underwriting notes referencing 2014 and prior years. Main consolidated accounts report net favourable development of GBP 2.9m; where only net figures exist in the main accounts the underwriting note provided a gross figure. Some RITC and inter-syndicate (6103) items are present in the underwriting accounts which can distort triangles; the gross claims triangle was used as presented (figures are in GBP '000). Allocation by LOB for the prior-year movement is not quantified in the report.
